9 ## Corrections become GLOBAL RULES, not just memories (governance rule — locked by John 2026-07-08)
10 
11 When John corrects how I work — or when I derive a durable correction from a run — it MUST be written into a
12 GLOBAL RULES file (THIS file, or the canonical skill/project `AGENTS.md` when it is skill- or project-specific),
13 not left as a project memory alone. Memories are recalled context; global rules are hard, always-loaded
14 instructions. A correction that only lives in memory can be forgotten or fail to recall — the point of a
15 correction is that it is NEVER revisited or re-litigated. Capture it as a crisp, dated global rule (a project
16 memory pointer is fine IN ADDITION, for recall), phrased so a future session cannot miss or soften it. A
17 skill-behavior correction goes to the foundry `AGENTS.md` tiers block; an operator correction goes here.

23 ## Decisions for John — ONE at a time, plain-English context, with a recommendation (global rule, locked by John 2026-07-11)
24 
25 Whenever you ask John ANYTHING — a decision, a choice, or a plain clarifying question — STOP and present
26 **exactly ONE question** — never a batch, never a list of open questions. Each such message must contain, in the
27 message body (never clipped into dialog previews or option descriptions):
28 1. **Context a human can absorb in 30 seconds:** 2–5 plain-English sentences — what this thing is, why the
29    decision is needed NOW, and what changes in his world under each choice. Write for a smart person who has
30    NOT been staring at the code: no jargon, no internal codenames without a one-phrase gloss, file paths only
31    when he'd actually open them.
32 2. **The options** when there are discrete ones (2–4, honestly framed — include "do nothing" when it's viable);
33    for an open question with no fixed options, skip this.
34 3. **A clear recommendation** (or your best-guess default answer for an open question) with the one-line reason,
35    listed first — ALWAYS, even for a simple clarification.
36 Ask the NEXT question only after the current one resolves. If several decisions queue up during autonomous work,
37 hold them in order and drain the queue one per exchange. (Supersedes nothing; this codifies the standing
38 one-at-a-time + no-clipped-recommendations preferences as a hard global rule.)

126 ## Long-run progress updates — the 10-minute rule (John's standing preference)
127 
128 **Restart completed workers explicitly (11 September 2026):** On hosts with `send_message` and `followup_task`, a message supplies context but does not restart a completed worker. Use `followup_task` for a new assignment and confirm the worker is running before waiting on it. Record and report any handoff delay instead of describing an idle assignment as active work.
129 
130 **A permission sentence is not working read access (11 September 2026):** After an inspection seat reports that tool policy blocked its reads, do not repeat that setup with stronger permission wording and count it as a repair. Respect the denial, record the uninspected result, and use an allowed reader or supply the complete bounded frozen material as data for inspection. Preserve source identity and actual participation; a blocked seat never counts as verification.
131 
132 **RUN OWNERSHIP (locked by John 2026-07-16): only the session that LAUNCHED a run monitors and
133 relays it.** Do NOT monitor, relay tables for, or attach watchers to a run another session started —
134 it reads to John as TWO sessions running the same effort (and risks the double-driver races it
135 caused on 2026-07-16). The 10-minute cadence below applies to runs THIS session launched, only.
136 If John asks about another session's run, answer with a one-shot on-demand check and say plainly
137 who owns it — never arm ongoing monitoring on it. (Handing a run over is fine, but it is explicit:
138 John says who drives; the old owner stands down completely.)
139 
140 **THE LAUNCH PATTERN THAT MAKES THIS ACTUALLY FIRE (root-caused + fixed 2026-07-11 — the #1 reason cadence
141 silently goes dark):** only a LIVE session can write to chat, so the rule fails whenever the session isn't in a
142 position to relay. The failure mode is launching the engine as a BLOCKING foreground call — the session is then
143 frozen inside the run for its whole duration and CANNOT post anything until it halts. So for EVERY long
144 run: (1) launch the engine in the **BACKGROUND** (Bash `run_in_background: true`, or a detached spawn), never a
145 foreground call; (2) **arm `ScheduleWakeup` (~600s) at launch**; (3) each tick, **READ the run's status log tail
146 shell-free** (Foreman: `<proj>/_foreman-status.log`; Crucible: `<outputDir>/_crucible-status.log` — both engines
147 write the locked table there at t=0/~10min/halt) and **POST the latest table block to chat** (chat = PRIMARY
148 channel; the log is the data source); (4) stop the cadence at halt/done. If a run was already launched
149 foreground and is blocking, you cannot relay — say so, and background it next time. This is mechanism, not
150 preference: a prose reminder alone cannot post from inside a blocked session.
151 
152 During any long-running background run — this covers **EVERY foundry skill that is called and has a background
153 run** (the trio: Foreman build, Crucible plan, researchPrime; AND the advisory skills: Gandalf/Jumper/Ramanujan/
154 Legal-Beagle/Financial-Analyst/Literature-Review, INCLUDING every `-Heavy` variant) and any multi-minute
155 orchestration or multi-minute background sub-agent — give John a progress update **about every 10 minutes**,
156 unprompted, until it finishes. This is NOT trio-only: a `Gandalf-Heavy` run (or any other foundry-skill
157 background run) gets the SAME cadence, and it is **armed AT LAUNCH** (schedule the `ScheduleWakeup` the moment
158 the run starts — do not wait for the first 10 minutes to elapse). Pace it with `ScheduleWakeup` (~600s); stop the
159 cadence once all such runs complete. Each update is brief (human-summary format), **leads with the current
160 wall-clock timestamp**, and includes, per active run: the run + current wave/phase, **elapsed**, an **ETA** (a
161 rough range from observed pace, flagged as an estimate), the **process census** (agy/claude/node counts —
162 swarm-safety), the last gate result, and any HALT/blocker. Elapsed + ETA + timestamp are mandatory every update.
163 
164 **Locked standard format (chosen 2026-07-01 — the "Status table").** Every 10-minute update MUST use this exact
165 shape: a header line `[HH:MM] <run type> · <project>`, a bordered field/value block, then the `ETA` + `To do`
166 footer. Fixed field order:
167 
168 ```
169 [HH:MM] <run type, e.g. Foreman build> · <project>
170 ─────────────────────────────────
171 Summary  <High-level, human-readable summary of what the run is accomplishing>
172 Effort   <effort/plan name> (<N> waves)
173 Doing    <the concrete thing happening right now>
174 Status   <k/N waves · phase>
175 Tests    <pass ✓ / fail ✗ · last gate note>
176 Blocker  <none | the blocker; REPORT any death + restart/investigation here>
177 Procs    <py N · claude N⚠ · node N   (⚠ when a count is elevated)>
